newsitem.title: USA: CME could adopt French trade system in 2nd half 98.
newsitem.headline: CME could adopt French trade system in 2nd half 98.

text.p: Chicago Mercantile Exchange officials said Thursday the CME could switch during the second half of 1998 to a French electronic system that would supplant the existing GLOBEX mechanism for after-hours futures trading.
"We would think probably in the second half of 1998 that we would be on the (French) trading system," CME president Rick Kilcollin said at a joint news conference here.

The CME and New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) said they had signed a letter of intent to adopt the NSC screen-based trading system created by the computerized SBF-Paris Bourse and the French futures and options exchange Matif SA.

In return, the Paris markets will adopt the Clearing 21 trade processing system the CME and NYMEX began developing more than five years ago to further automate clearing and help cut costs for the exchanges and their member firms.
CME heads said they have until May 31 to convert the letter into a legal contract, and the final agreement must be approved by each exchange's board of directors.
CME chairman emeritus Leo Melamed said the exchanges during the next two months must negotiate specific terms of the agreement, including financing and rights issues.

"We're very pleased with this result. But...we have some negotiations to do," Melamed cautioned. "And so there's no guarantee that we will produce an agreement. But everyone to this letter of intent believes we will."

Under the plan, which CME said was cobbled together during the last couple of weeks, GLOBEX would retain its name but switch to the NSC system. Melamed said the CME and Matif envisioned moving onto the NSC system at the same time.

Earlier this month, Reuters Holdings Plc said the GLOBEX system built with the CME and Matif was unlikely to continue operations beyond 1998. The contract linking Reuters, the CME and Matif expires in April 1998.

But CME chairman Jack Sandner said the CME on Wednesday had asked Reuters for an extension of the contract past April 1998 to give it enough time to switch GLOBEX to the NSC system. He said Reuters had taken the issue "under advisement."
"As I understand it, that is accurate," a Reuters spokesman said in response to an inquiry. "But we would have nothing to add to what Mr Sandner had to say at this point."

The CME said the new agreement, which it doubted would encounter any unique regulatory hurdles, would let users route orders to the trading floor during daytime hours and then switch to after-hours GLOBEX trading using the same terminals.
The CME also said the new effort might advance the plan it announced last week with the Chicago Board of Trade to pursue consolidating the two exchanges' clearing functions.

"It certainly advances that idea. I think overall, the thrust to have common clearing between the Chicago Board of Trade and Chicago Mercantile Exchange has so many going-points for it that it doesn't need any additional impetus to do it," Melamed said. "And so whether we use the Clearing 21 or whatever clearing system is used, it's going to serve the community of users and so I think that goes on its own track and I think it's moving forward."
